_doc: The first-day tutorial of each birth chain (clarity pass, docs/CLARITY.md §2). `chains` lists the stages of a chain in order; `text` is a flat dictionary: `stage.part` keys, with a `chain:` prefix for a variant that only that chain uses. Placeholders: {head} {headFull} {headDesc} {headRel} {meet} {meetDesc} {village} {home} {place} {strip} {nb} {nbDesc} {shop} {shopDesc} {keeper} {church} {priest} {priestDesc} {steward} {stewardDesc} {peer} {peerDesc} {pay} {label}. A stage is skipped when it cannot be made for this player (no neighbour, no shop …).

text.meet.title: Meet your family
text.meet.why: {meet} will tell you what the day holds. Say good morning first.
text.meet.talk.hint: Walk up to {meet} (W A S D to walk, drag with the right mouse button to look round) and press E, or click them.
text.baron:meet.why: {meet} will want to see you before the household's day begins.
text.noble:meet.why: {meet} will want to see you before the household's day begins.
text.work.title: Lend a hand at home
text.farm:work.why.craft: {head} keeps the household fed by many small crafts: brewing, baking, spinning. Every batch you make is one less to buy.
text.work.why.strip: {head}: 'The land will not work itself.' Every task you finish leaves the strip a step further along.
text.work.why.garden: The beds feed the pot between harvests, and {head} has no time to weed them.
text.work.why.stock: The animals must be seen to every day, and {head} has a hundred other things to do.
text.work.why.herd: The village beasts must be driven out to the common pasture, and someone has to mind them there.
text.work.why.craft: {head} needs the bench kept busy: finished work is coin, and your hands learn the trade.
text.craft:work.why.craft: {head} keeps the household by the workshop. The first thing to learn is the bench.
text.work.why.barn: The sheaves are stacked in the barn. Until they are threshed and winnowed they are straw, not bread.
text.work.why.dig: Stone sells, and the quarry is open to any with a pick.
text.work.go.hint: Follow the golden beacon. When you are close the prompt at the bottom of the screen shows what E will do.
text.work.go.hint.strip: Follow the golden beacon and stand on the strip itself. The prompt at the bottom of the screen shows what E will do.
text.work.do.hint: Face it and press E, or click it. Keep at it: each bout fills the bar and teaches a little.
text.work.do.hint.strip: Press E, or click the strip. Each press is a bout of work; keep going until the strip is done.
text.jobs.title: Look for work
text.jobs.why: There is little for you to do at {home}. A post earns coin and teaches a trade, and someone in {village} is hiring.
text.jobs.go.hint: Follow the golden beacon to the door.
text.jobs.ask.hint: Press E at the door and choose 'Ask about work', or hold E for the wheel. The list shows what each post pays and what it asks of you.
text.jobs.reward: A post to take, when you are ready
text.errand.title: A neighbour's errand
text.errand.why: A willing pair of legs earns a penny and a friend. {nb} lives close by.
text.errand.do.hint: Walk up to {nb}, hold E to open the action wheel, and choose 'Run an errand'.
text.errand.reward: A penny or two, and {nb}'s thanks
text.noble:errand.why: A page learns the household by carrying its messages. {nb} has something to be taken across the way, and a coin for the trouble.
text.baron:errand.why: An heir who has never carried a message does not know what a message costs. {nb} has one, and a coin for the trouble.
text.trade.title: Buy or sell something
text.trade.why: Coin changes hands wherever people meet. See what {shop} will pay for your goods, or what they ask.
text.merchant:trade.why: A merchant's child learns by haggling. See what the stalls pay for the bread and ale in your pack, or what they ask.
text.trade.do.hint: Press E and choose Trade. Sell the bread or ale in your pack, or buy something: either counts.
text.noble:trade.why: A lord who never bought or sold anything is cheated by every steward. See what {shop} gives for the bread and ale in your pack, or asks for its own.
text.baron:trade.why: A lord who never bought or sold anything is cheated by every steward. See what {shop} gives for the bread and ale in your pack, or asks for its own.
text.chapel.title: Prayers at the chapel
text.chapel.why: A household of quality begins and ends its day at church, and the priest notes who is missing.
text.chapel.go.hint: Follow the golden beacon to the door.
text.chapel.pray.hint: Hold E at the church and choose 'Pray'. On a holy morning you may hear Mass instead.
text.chapel.mass.hint: Hold E at the church and choose 'Hear Mass'.
text.chapel.reward: A good name with the parish
text.lessons.title: Lessons from the priest
text.lessons.why: Letters open doors that swords do not: a lord's son who can read is a lord who cannot be cheated.
text.lessons.talk.hint: Press E to talk, then 'Ask a favour' and ask for lessons in letters.
text.steward.title: Meet the steward
text.steward.why: A baron's heir must know who keeps the accounts, and the steward knows where every penny goes.
text.steward.talk.hint: Press E to talk. Ask about the lands and the people.
text.folk.title: Know your people
text.folk.why: Those who till your father's land are your future tenants. Learn their faces and their names.
text.folk.talk.text: Speak with two of your people
text.folk.talk.hint: Walk up to anyone in the village and press E. Their nameplate shows who they are and how they stand to you.
text.night.title: Home before dark
text.night.why: The day is done when you say it is. Sleep at home and the morning brings fresh work, and a summary of what you achieved.
text.night.home.hint: Follow the golden beacon. The door glows when you are near.
text.night.sleep.hint: Hold E at the door and choose 'Sleep until dawn', or press Z.
text.night.reward: A summary of your day, and a fresh morning
text.lord:steward.why: Your steward keeps the accounts and knows every field and every debt of {village}. Hear his report before you give your first orders.
text.lord:steward.talk.hint: Walk up to the steward and press E (or click him). Ask about the lands and the people.
text.plan.title: Set your fields and labour
text.plan.why: The manor lives on its fields. Name what each field will grow, and decide how much of your serfs' week-work goes to building instead of the demesne.
text.plan.do.text: Open the ruler's seat (U) and give an order under Fields & labour
text.plan.do.hint: Press U. Under Fields & labour, choose a crop for a field's next sowing, or move the slider for labour sent to your works.
text.plan.reward: A manor that works to your plan
text.command.title: Put your purse to work
text.command.why: Coin in a chest builds nothing. Set a man to research, raise soldiers, or tell your steward what to sell.
text.command.do.text: In the ruler's seat (U), begin research, raise men, or give a trade order
text.command.do.hint: Press U, then use Research, Men & arms or Trade orders. A greyed-out choice says what it still needs.
text.command.reward: The first works of your rule
text.train.title: Make yourself strong
text.train.why: A lord who cannot fight is a lord on borrowed time. Your own arm counts: drill at the training yard.
text.train.go.text: Go to the training yard of {village}
text.train.do.hint: Stand in the yard and press E (or click the yard), then choose 'Drill at the pell'. Melee, Strength and Endurance grow.
text.train.reward: Melee practice, and the respect of your men
text.lord:folk.why: These are your people. Learn their faces and their names; a lord who is known is obeyed more gladly.
text.lord:meet.why: Your household will want to see you before the day begins.
